countedBy: lane landmarks-r19-a-20261127 from the whole-face rectified crop of the 27.3 m Rokin front out of recording_2025-06-16_06-42-40_01743 (2025, 36 px/m), checked against TMX7316010203-000709_pano_0000_001134 (2018); not yet blind-counted. Glazed openings bottom row first; solid doors and the red shutter do not count; lights split by mullions narrower than 0.3 m are one opening. alongM: the silhouette's viewer-left edge is the cream house's south flank roof, 0.35 m south of the front's south corner; the house lines are the crop's (cream 0-5.42 m, black 5.42-10.63 m, Hajenius 10.63-27.33 m).

facades.name: Hajenius front
facades.note: Openings are the glass and the cream sun blinds drawn down over it in both crops (the blinds are part of each window). Bands: the two outer bays' shop windows behind the red awnings (the middle bay's red shutter does not count); the north bay's row of three small lights over its wooden door (3.2-4.4 m, one ribbon); the wide windows at 5.3-7.8 m, one per bay; three storeys of one opening per bay (the outer bays' narrow-wide-narrow lights stand between mullions about 0.22 m wide, one ribbon); on the mansard the three dormers and the end gable's oculus. Axes: the three bays and the north end bay. Not symmetric: the narrower end bay under its gable.

facades.name: Black house
facades.note: The black neck-gable house between the cream house and Hajenius: the shopfront under the red fascia, three storeys of two sash windows; the hoisting window in the neck is a white panel and does not count. Columns: the two window axes and the shopfront's centre between them.

facades.name: Cream house
facades.note: The cream bell-gable house on the lane corner: the shop window, the three transom lights over the sign, three storeys of three lights (the fourth-storey ones round-headed under the half-round markies) and the gable's pair of lights. Columns: the three light axes (the shop window on the middle one) and the gable's pair of lights, which stand 1.1 m either side of the centre, between them.
